implementation_notes: Default C realization where Kafka is the transport: the group id is the durable subscription identity and the committed offset is the retained position, bounded by the cluster's offset retention. Choose it when the log already holds the events; poll-commit discipline then decides whether the backlog is replayed or lost.
pitfalls: Offsets are only a position, not a message store: if the log has compacted or aged out past the committed offset the consumer cannot recover the gap.
Committing from a second thread races with the poll loop; librdkafka handles are not thread-safe.

variants.name: MQTT persistent session on Mosquitto (libmosquitto)
variants.idiom_name: libmosquitto mosquitto_connect with clean session disabled and a stable client id
variants.implementation_notes: Where MQTT is the transport, durability is the broker-held session: connect with clean session disabled and a stable client id and the broker queues QoS 1/2 publications while the client is offline. Mosquitto only keeps those sessions if persistence is enabled, and caps their lifetime with persistent_client_expiration, so the retention half of the pattern is entirely broker configuration.
pitfalls: Mosquitto defaults to persistence disabled and to no offline-session cap, so 'durable' sessions may be memory-only or never expire.
QoS 0 publications are never queued, and reconnecting with a fresh client id drops the old session's queued messages.
